title: Career Confidence & Communication
description: Companion-coach pack for working life: imposter syndrome, telling your wins, taking feedback, landing well in a new role. Scenario problems graded on rubric; the tutor rehearses with you, then coaches.

skills.title: Telling your wins as STAR stories

problems.prompt: You just started the job and a voice in your head says "they're going to find out I'm not good enough." Write what you would say back to that voice, in your own words.

criteria: names the feeling without judging it
answers it with concrete evidence of competence
realistic, not cheerleading
written in the first person

problems.prompt: Tell me about a time you solved a hard problem. Give it as a STAR story: situation, task, action, result.

criteria: all four STAR parts present and in order
the result is specific or measured
under 150 words
sounds like you, not a template

problems.prompt: Your manager says your report "missed the mark" and gives no detail. Draft the exact next question you would ask.

criteria: asks for a specific example
zero defensiveness
invites the manager to say what good looks like
one short question, not a speech

problems.prompt: Draft the 30-day slice of a first-90-days plan for your new role: what you will learn, who you will meet, and one small win you will aim for.

criteria: a learning goal
a relationship goal with named kinds of people
one realistic quick win
scope a real person could do in 30 days

problems.prompt: A colleague gets public praise for work you contributed to. What do you actually do next?

criteria: assumes good intent first
advocates for yourself with facts, not accusation
picks a concrete moment or channel to do it
keeps the working relationship intact

problems.prompt: You step into the lift with a senior leader. Introduce yourself in two sentences.

criteria: role and the value you add, stated plainly
opens a door for follow-up
no filler
exactly two sentences
